---
title: "Plasma PfHRP2 and Peripheral Parasitaemia"
output: github_document
---

```{r include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

This plot shows the relationship between plasma PfHRP2 concentration and observed
peripheral parasitaemia in AQUAMAT patients with matched positive measurements.

Peripheral parasitaemia measures the density of parasites circulating in peripheral
blood, whereas plasma PfHRP2 provides information about the larger parasite biomass.
PfHRP2 released by infected erythrocytes persists in the circulation and can therefore
reflect parasite biomass that is not represented by the contemporaneous peripheral
parasite count, including parasites sequestered from the peripheral circulation. The
comparison is motivated by Dondorp et al. (2005), who used plasma PfHRP2 to estimate
total parasite biomass in falciparum malaria and contrasted this with circulating
parasite biomass estimated from peripheral parasitaemia.

Both variables span several orders of magnitude and are therefore shown on logarithmic
axes. The fitted line represents a linear regression of log10 plasma PfHRP2 on log10
peripheral parasitaemia, with the shaded region showing the 95% confidence interval.
Pearson and Spearman correlations were also calculated to quantify the strength of
the association.

```{r load = FALSE}
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

DATA_FILE <- "Data/dat_all.csv"
dat_all <- fread(DATA_FILE)
```

```{r prep = FALSE}
# ---- Retain matched positive AQUAMAT measurements ----
AQ_hrp2_para <- dat_all[Trial == "AQUAMAT" & is.finite(parasitaemia) &
                        is.finite(hrp2_plasma) & parasitaemia > 0 &
                        hrp2_plasma > 0, .(ID, parasitaemia, hrp2_plasma)]

# ---- Log10-transform both variables ----
AQ_hrp2_para[, log10_parasitaemia := log10(parasitaemia)]
AQ_hrp2_para[, log10_hrp2 := log10(hrp2_plasma)]
```

```{r analysis = FALSE}
# ---- Log-log linear regression ----
hrp2_model <- lm(log10_hrp2 ~ log10_parasitaemia, data = AQ_hrp2_para)
model_summary <- summary(hrp2_model)

intercept <- unname(coef(hrp2_model)[1])
slope <- unname(coef(hrp2_model)[2])
r_squared <- model_summary$r.squared

# ---- Pearson correlation on log10-transformed variables ----
correlation_test <- cor.test(AQ_hrp2_para$log10_parasitaemia, AQ_hrp2_para$log10_hrp2,
                             method = "pearson")

pearson_r <- unname(correlation_test$estimate)
correlation_p <- correlation_test$p.value

# ---- Spearman rank correlation ----
spearman_test <- cor.test(AQ_hrp2_para$log10_parasitaemia, AQ_hrp2_para$log10_hrp2,
                          method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

spearman_rho <- unname(spearman_test$estimate)
spearman_p <- spearman_test$p.value

# ---- Format p-value for display ----
format_p <- function(p) {
  if (p < 0.001) {
    return("< 0.001")
  }
  paste0("= ", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3))
}
```

```{r plot, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# ---- State IDDO AQUAMAT colours ----
AQ_colour <- "#E31B23"
AQ_light <- "#EC767D"

# ---- Plot on log10-transformed coordinates ----
plot_hrp2_para <- ggplot(AQ_hrp2_para, aes(x = log10_parasitaemia, y = log10_hrp2)) +
  geom_point(colour = AQ_colour, alpha = 0.35, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = AQ_colour, fill = AQ_light,
              alpha = 0.25, linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(floor(min(AQ_hrp2_para$log10_parasitaemia)),
                                  ceiling(max(AQ_hrp2_para$log10_parasitaemia)), by = 1),
    labels = function(x) scales::label_comma()(10^x), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(floor(min(AQ_hrp2_para$log10_hrp2)),
                                  ceiling(max(AQ_hrp2_para$log10_hrp2)), by = 1),
    labels = function(x) scales::label_comma()(10^x), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = range(AQ_hrp2_para$log10_parasitaemia),
                  ylim = range(AQ_hrp2_para$log10_hrp2)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  xlab(expression(paste("Peripheral parasitaemia (parasites/", mu, "L)"))) +
  ylab("Plasma PfHRP2 (ng/mL)") +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 8, 8))

print(plot_hrp2_para)
```

Plasma PfHRP2 concentration was only weakly correlated with peripheral parasitaemia
in AQUAMAT despite the large sample size (n = 3,291; Pearson r = 0.110, p < 0.001;
Spearman rho = 0.105, p < 0.001). In a log10-log10 linear regression, a 10-fold
increase in peripheral parasitaemia was associated with only a 1.20-fold increase
in fitted plasma PfHRP2 concentration, and peripheral parasitaemia explained 1.2%
of the variation in log10 PfHRP2 (R² = 0.012). The wide variation in PfHRP2
concentration among patients with similar peripheral parasite densities is
consistent with the two measurements capturing different aspects of parasite
burden.
